title: Drone Report and TRJ-01: Oil Past Mill Ridge Ramp

fields.incidentName: Prairie Line MP 214.3 Kansas River Crossing Release
fields.observer: Deputy R. Okafor, Prairie Bend County Sheriff's Office (photo and drone stills forwarded by Prairie Bend County Emergency Management at 0708)
fields.platform: Sheriff's Office small drone, call sign PBSO UAS 2, launched from the Mill Ridge boat ramp lot
fields.conditions: Clear; visibility 10 mi; wind S 5 kt; river about 8,500 cfs, current about 2 kt; low sun from the east is causing glare on the downstream reach; strong rotten-egg odor at the ramp

observations.position: Drainage ditch, north bank, upstream of the Mill Ridge boat ramp (river mile 0)
observations.appearance: Black crude, continuous flow; pooled at the culvert outfall
observations.extent: About 300 ft of ditch visibly oiled, bank to bank
observations.movement: Still discharging into the river at the culvert mouth

observations.position: Culvert outfall to Kansas River, river mile 0
observations.appearance: Black, thick oil at the bank, turning brown about 50 ft offshore
observations.extent: Patch about 40 x 80 ft along the north bank
observations.movement: Pulled downstream by the current; some held in the eddy below the outfall

observations.position: Mill Ridge boat ramp, river mile 0.2
observations.appearance: Dark brown to black band with rainbow sheen along both edges
observations.extent: About 60 ft wide, covering the north half of the channel
observations.movement: Downstream at current speed, toward the bend below the ramp

observations.appearance: Broken brown streaks and rainbow sheen, with silver sheen at the leading edge
observations.extent: Streaks 10 to 30 ft wide spread over about 0.3 mi
observations.movement: Leading edge moving downstream toward the Kaw Valley Fishing Access; the outside of the bend has the most coverage

fields.wildlife: Two fishermen standing on the Mill Ridge boat ramp within about 20 ft of the oiled water; no boats on the water. One great blue heron on the south bank sandbar at the bend; not visibly oiled. Swallows feeding low over the river near the ramp. No dead fish seen. No response vessels or boom on scene.
fields.recommendations:
Keep the public off the Mill Ridge ramp and away from the ditch until the Kansas Department of Wildlife and Parks closure is in place. Check air for H2S before anyone works at the ditch or outfall. Fly the piping plover sandbars (miles 6 to 9) at about 0830 to catch the leading edge.

TRAJECTORY PRODUCT TRJ-01. NOAA Scientific Support Coordinator (SimCell). Model run 0705 CDT, 06/08/2027. Basis: oil entered the river about 0640; surface velocity 2.3 mph; ±20% wind band; flow 8,500 cfs. LEADING-EDGE ARRIVAL WINDOWS: Miles 0–3, Mill Ridge ramp and Kaw Valley Fishing Access: 0640–0800 (ARRIVED). Miles 6–9, piping plover sandbars: 0850–1125. Mile 11, Prairie Bend Rural Water District intake (6,200 customers): 1040–1225. Mile 22, Cottonwood Slough mussel bed: 1440–1810. Mile 34, Sterling Bluff Water Department intake (41,000 customers): 1900 Tue – 0025 Wed 9 June. Next rerun 1305 CDT, or sooner if river flow changes by more than 15%.

instructorNote: This inject confirms that oil is in the river and gives the arrival time windows for each site, so the talk of an instrument glitch from I-07 should stop. Watch for the Environmental Unit Leader to send TRJ-01 out with its run time and rank the intakes first, then the plovers and the mussel bed. The QI should share it with Unified Command, and the OSRO should plan angled boom against the windows. The Sterling Bluff Director should work out that closure must be complete by 18:00 (start by about 17:00), and someone should flag that the rural water district has to decide by about 09:40. That decision belongs to the utilities, not to Ironbark.
